summary: Account and project professional with 5 years in a regulated, multi-country payments business (Global Blue, part of Shift4), promoted three times in four years. Runs partner and account governance across ~40 countries, keeps service data accurate, and fixes systemic issues that span several systems and owners. Leads through influence: decision packs, risk escalation to accountable owners, and training that raises team standards.
cover_letter: I am applying for the Partner Estate & Relationship Manager role at Monzo. The role is about governing a partner estate, spotting systemic issues in service performance and getting several parties to fix them. That is the core of my work at Global Blue, part of Shift4, a regulated payments business where I have been promoted three times in four years.

I run a 25-country account governance review cycle with every review held on schedule: I set the timeline, prepare the decision packs and escalate risks to accountable owners. When a major retail client's invoice reporting had been failing for five months, I traced the fault across three systems and coordinated the fix with four system owners. I also keep a ~600-account master list accurate for account managers in ~40 countries, and built the issue-ratio and eligibility monitoring now used in every monthly business review.

I lead mostly through influence. I run training and briefings for account managers, country teams and new starters, and I wrote the onboarding playbook that two global account teams adopted as standard. I would bring the same rigour and constructive challenge to Monzo's partners, and I am keen to learn your partner tooling quickly.
I would welcome the chance to discuss how I could help Monzo's partner estate run smoothly.

answers.Why Monzo?: I want to apply the partner governance and issue-resolution work I do in regulated payments to a bank whose customer focus I admire, in a remote-first role.
